messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D marble parkour game for phones/tablets with timed courses, map building, leaderboards, ghost competition, and shareable custom maps.
- The project was empty and is being built from scratch as a static Three.js/Vite web game.

## Requirements
- 3D marble parkour gameplay with timed maps.
- Map builder for custom courses.
- Competition via leaderboards/ghosts; maps timed.
- Must work on phone/tablet with touch controls and responsive layout.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) for checks and read only the latest one; full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them at the end.

## Decisions
- Plain Vite + Three.js project, fully client-side/offline, persistence via `localStorage`.
- Competition implemented locally: seeded rival times for built-in maps, best-time ghost replay, and shareable challenge codes carrying the creator's target time.
- Built-in courses: “Sunrise Sprint”, “Neon Current”, “Sky Temple”; custom maps can be shared/imported as `MR1.` codes.
- Map builder is grid/level based with platform, ramp, beam, spinner, mover, boost, bounce, checkpoint, start, finish, and erase tools.
- Touch controls: virtual joystick, jump button, optional tilt steering; keyboard `WASD`/arrows + `Space` on desktop.
- Self-hosted fonts downloaded to `public/fonts/`.
- Assumptions to state when finished: no server/network accounts, leaderboards/ghosts are local, custom-map sharing is via copy/paste codes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created project scaffold: `package.json`, `index.html`, `src/`.
- Installed Three.js/Vite dependencies.
- Downloaded and wired local fonts.
- Implemented `src/maps.js` with themes, built-in maps, helper functions, starter map.
- Implemented `src/store.js` persistence, records/ghosts, leaderboard, time formatting, share-code encode/decode.
- Implemented `src/audio.js` procedural WebAudio effects.
- Implemented most of `src/game.js`: renderer, themes, sky/clouds/stars, showcase scene, course construction, all piece types, collision physics, marble, ghost playback, race lifecycle, builder rendering/placement, camera, debug API.
- Wrote `index.html` full UI structure: home, map select, HUD, pause, results, builder, modals, toast.
- Wrote `src/style.css` responsive/mobile styling and component styles.
- Wrote most of `src/main.js`: map thumbnails/cards, navigation, race flow, results, builder flow, save/share/import, settings/tilt/sound, input handling, boot loop.

### Active
- Continuing to finish and validate `src/main.js`; the last edit appended settings/input/boot wiring.
- No build or browser test has been run yet.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; next work is syntax/runtime validation and visual/gameplay testing.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` or start Vite to catch syntax/import/runtime errors.
2. Inspect `src/game.js` for known issues: `updateDynamics` signature, countdown reset on resume, finish recording, ghost path height, builder camera preservation, `showcaseSparks`, mover velocity.
3. Fix all compile/runtime errors, then launch a server and capture a home-screen screenshot.
4. Test navigation to map select, start a race, move/jump, verify HUD/countdown/results.
5. Test builder: place/erase pieces, level changes, undo, save, test, import/share code.
6. Validate mobile layout and touch controls with Playwright at ~390×844 and desktop.
7. Check screenshots (small JPEGs) for visual quality, then note assumptions in final response.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: main app/UI/input flow; most likely place for remaining bugs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Three.js renderer, physics, courses, builder internals, camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full DOM/UI structure and screen IDs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: responsive styling; recently patched pointer-events, result layout, builder warnings.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/maps.js`: built-in course definitions, themes, piece metadata, `CELL`/`STEP` constants.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/store.js`: localStorage, leaderboard, share-code codec.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural sound engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite/Three dependencies and scripts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/public/fonts/baloo2.woff2`: display font.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/public/fonts/outfit.woff2`: body font.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; git repo; changes are uncommitted.
- Start server: `npm run dev` (Vite) or `./start.sh` (runtime builds/serves static output).
- `playwright-cli` and Playwright Chromium are available; AGENTS.md says use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, but the project server may use another port—check.
- `window.MarbleRush = { game, store }` and `window.__marble = game` are exposed for debugging.
- Game exposes `debugGo()`, `debugTeleport(x,y,z)`, `debugFinish()`, `debugState()`.
- Critical known bug candidates:
  - `game.js` `finishRace()` originally referenced a nonexistent `this.recordMinutes`; patched to plain `recording: this.recording.slice()`.
  - `updateRace()` countdown end previously reset `raceTime` on resume; patched using `this.resuming`.
  - `recordSample` now takes `dt` and `finishRace` calls `recordSample(0, true)`.
  - `updateDynamics(time, dt)` now divides mover delta by `safeDt`.
  - `clearWorld()` now calls `clearShowcase()`.
  - `ghostEnabled` is set from `startRace` via `opts.ghost`? Check: game.startRace currently sets ghost path but may not assign `this.ghostEnabled`; main sets `game.ghostEnabled = !!s.ghost` at boot and on toggle. Verify `updateGhost()` respects `ghostEnabled`.
- `main.js` uses `formatDelta`, `leaderboardFor`, `rankFor`, etc. Ensure all imported symbols exist.
- Potential issue: `handleMapAction` uses `openBuilder(map, { editingId: map.id, origin: 'maps' })`; `openBuilder` accepts `opts.editingId` correctly.
- Potential issue: `main.js` calls `openMaps()` in `nextCourse`; defined near the end as `function openMaps(tab = currentTab) { showMaps(tab); }`.
- Potential issue: `main.js` references `lastTimerText` before its `let` declaration at runtime? It is declared after `updateTimerHud` definition but initialized before boot/loop; function hoisting is fine, TDZ only matters at call time after declaration executes.
- `index.html` result card now has `.result-top` wrapper.
- CSS pointer-events: `#ui` is `pointer-events:none`; `.hero`, `.sheet`, `.topbar`, `.home-footer`, `.modal-layer`, `.overlay-screen`, `.builder-top/bottom/level`, `.toast` set auto; verify all needed controls remain clickable.
- The map thumbnail code uses `ctx.roundRect`, supported by current Chromium.
- Built-in map coordinates use direction mapping `0=+Z, 1=+X, 2=-Z, 3=-X`; `yawFor(r) = r*π/2`.
- Physics constants: marble radius 0.5, cell 2.4, level step 1.2, gravity 26, jump 8.1, max speed 10.8.
- Final summary should mention: built-in courses, builder, local leaderboard/rival times, ghost replay, share codes, tilt/joystick controls, and that data never leaves the device.

- This aligns the camera behind the direction of travel. Because input is camera-relative, the direction of travel is initially the input direction. As the camera rotates, the forward vector rotates, so the same joystick input steers the ball in a new direction, causing a curving path. Hmm, but if the joystick is held up, the desired yaw = current camYaw (since velocity = forward), so no rotation. Only when velocity has a lateral component (pushing diagonally) does the camera rotate to align behind the diagonal movement; that would then cause the ball to curve further, spiraling. Bad.

Alternative: auto-follow toward the course direction (tangent), not the velocity. We can compute a "track direction" from the current map piece? Too complex.

Alternative: auto-rotate camera to keep behind the ball's *positional progress* along the course's next checkpoint/finish. Compute direction from ball to the next checkpoint or finish, and gently yaw the camera toward it. This would keep the camera facing along the course. As the player turns, the camera aligns with the course. Input is camera-relative, and the camera gradually points down the course, so pushing up follows the course. This is good! But the next checkpoint may be far and require detours. The course is mostly linear; the nearest checkpoint or finish direction is a decent guide. Use the finish direction when no checkpoints. For maps with gaps, the direction is still along the route.

```
if (this.userOrbitHold <= 0 && this.ball.speed > 1.5) {
  const target = this.nextCheckpointTarget();
  if (target) {
    const dx = target.x - ball.x, dz = target.z - ball.z;
    if (dx*dx+dz*dz > 1) {
      const desired = Math.atan2(-dx, -dz); // yaw such that forward = (-sin yaw, -cos yaw) = normalized(dx,dz)
      let diff = normalizeAngle(desired - camYaw);
      this.camYaw += diff * (1 - Math.exp(-1.1*dt));
    }
  }
}
```

But the camera should be behind the ball looking toward the target, so the camera position is target + offset at yaw; the offset uses (sin yaw, ..., cos yaw) * dist → the camera is behind relative to forward (which is -sin,-cos). Yes.

This will automatically rotate the camera toward the next checkpoint/finish. However, if the target is behind/beside, it can rotate quickly; slow rate 1.1/s. Since `userOrbitHold` is set to 2.4 on manual drag, manual control overrides for 2.4s. Good.

if (this.mode==='race' && this.raceState==='running' && this.userOrbitHold<=0) this.followCourse(dt);

- active checkpoints not yet active: pick the nearest (in course order). `this.checkpoints.find(cp=>!cp.active)` maybe the first unactivated. But if the player skips one, the next one is still the first unactivated, maybe behind. Use the first inactive checkpoint by index; if all active, finishInfo.

- Use only if distance > 2.5.

## Objective
- Finish the existing 3D marble parkour game so it is playable on phones and tablets, with timed courses, map building, and competition features.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project; do not ask clarifying questions and note reasonable assumptions when finished.
- Check the interface using small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px); read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal best-time ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the project scaffold, local fonts, built-in maps, persistence/share-code utilities, procedural audio, game/UI implementation, and responsive styling.
- Implemented core race and builder flows, including touch and keyboard controls.

### Active
- Continue from the existing implementation; validate and fix build, runtime, gameplay, builder, and mobile-layout issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and fix any compile or import errors.
2. Inspect `src/game.js` and `src/main.js` for runtime issues, then start the app and test navigation, racing, controls, results, and builder workflows.
3. Validate desktop and phone-sized layouts in a browser; save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize the finished features and note that competition and sharing are local/offline.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: UI navigation, race and builder flow, settings, and input handling.
- `src/game.js`: Three.js scene, physics, race lifecycle, ghost playback, and builder internals.
- `index.html`: Screen and UI structure.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive layout and component styling.
- `src/maps.js`: Built-in courses, themes, pieces, and starter map.
- `src/store.js`: Local persistence, records, leaderboard, and share-code utilities.
- `src/audio.js`: Procedural audio effects.
- `package.json`: Vite and Three.js dependencies and scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no build or browser validation has been run yet.
- Built-in courses are “Sunrise Sprint”, “Neon Current”, and “Sky Temple”; custom maps use `MR1.` share codes.
- Builder supports platform, ramp, beam, spinner, mover, boost, bounce, checkpoint, start, finish, and erase tools.
- Touch controls include a virtual joystick and jump button, with optional tilt; desktop uses WASD/arrows and Space.
- Verify that `startRace` sets `ghostEnabled` as expected and `updateGhost()` respects it; also test countdown/resume timing, finish recording, ghost height, builder camera preservation, `showcaseSparks`, and mover velocity.
- Debug hooks are exposed as `window.MarbleRush = { game, store }` and `window.__marble = game`; game helpers include `debugGo()`, `debugTeleport(x,y,z)`, `debugFinish()`, and `debugState()`.
- Assumptions to state at completion: no server or network accounts; leaderboards and ghosts are local, and custom-map sharing is via copy/paste codes.

## Objective
- Finish the existing 3D marble parkour game so it is playable on phones and tablets, with timed courses, map building, and competition features.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Check the interface using small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px); inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold, maps, persistence/share-code utilities, procedural audio, game/UI implementation, and responsive styling are present.
- Core race and builder flows, including touch and keyboard controls, are implemented.
- `npm run build` succeeds; Vite reports a warning that the JS bundle exceeds 500 kB.
- Browser smoke test on a 390×844 mobile viewport confirmed home, map selection with three cards, and race startup without page errors.

### Active
- Validate and fix pause/resume UI, gameplay controls, results, builder workflows, and responsive layouts.
- Inspect the requested current small JPEG screenshot; none has yet been successfully captured.

### Blocked
- Pause smoke test showed `raceState: "paused"` but `#screen-pause` remained hidden, so resume control could not be used. Investigate `showPause()` and related screen/HUD visibility logic.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `showPause()` and race screen transitions in `src/main.js`; reproduce and fix the hidden pause screen.
2. Run browser checks for movement, countdown/resume timing, finish recording, ghost visibility, and builder save/test/back flows.
3. Capture and inspect the latest mobile JPEG (viewport ≤1280px), then check desktop layout.
4. Rebuild and report completed features and local/offline competition/sharing assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: UI navigation, race and builder flow, settings, and input handling.
- `src/game.js`: Three.js scene, physics, race lifecycle, ghost playback, and builder internals.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive layout and component styling.
- `index.html`: Screen and UI structure.
- `src/maps.js`: Built-in courses, themes, pieces, and starter map.
- `src/store.js`: Local persistence, records, leaderboard, and share-code utilities.
- `package.json`: Vite and Three.js dependencies and scripts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. The latest build modified tracked `dist/index.html`, deleted `dist/assets/index-C-TzBNTR.js`, and created `dist/assets/index-CnwxJKc1.js`; inspect before deciding whether to retain or revert generated changes.
- Built-in courses are “Sunrise Sprint”, “Neon Current”, and “Sky Temple”; custom maps use `MR1.` share codes.

## Objective
- Finish and expand the existing 3D marble parkour game so it works well on phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Check the interface using small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px); inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.

- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.

# Inspection report: curved-piece integration

No files were modified. The current course pipeline supports piece types built from `{ t, x, z, l, r }`; there is no curved-piece type yet.

## Current structure

- **Piece types and course geometry —** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/maps.js:3–12`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/maps.js ) defines the grid constants and `PIECE_TYPES`; `courseBounds()` reads each piece’s grid coordinates and level at `:271–280`. Add a new type such as `'curve'` to the type list.
- **Rendering and colliders —** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js:739–748`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js ) creates box-collider records. `addSlab()` builds standard platform meshes and box colliders at `:760–802`; `createRamp()` shows the existing custom-geometry and oriented-collider pattern at `:804–831`. Piece rendering is dispatched in `buildPiece()` at `:1139–1159`, and `buildCourse()` calls it for each map piece at `:1256–1291`.
- **Builder preview and placement —** The editor’s generic ghost is constructed at [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js:1297–1348`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js ). `applyBuilderCursor()` handles ramp/beam previews and orientation at `:1422–1444`; hover positioning is at `:1463–1488`; placement creates `{ t, x, z, l, r }` at `:1490–1518`.
- **Collision processing —** The physics loop checks each collider at [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js:2044–2060`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js ). `resolveSphereBox()` handles oriented-box contact and response at `:2077–2152`; it does not require piece-specific collision logic for ordinary platforms.
- **Palette —** Piece icons and the `PIECES` palette entries are in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js:18–48`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js ). `buildPalette()` creates buttons from those entries at `:1460–1476`, so adding a palette item also requires an icon/label/hint.
- **Challenge codes —** Encoding serializes only `t,x,z,l,r` at [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/store.js:197–210`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/store.js ). The decoder’s accepted types and reconstruction are at `:213–235`.

A new palette item should fit the existing button treatment; no structural CSS change appears necessary.

1. Add `'curve'` to `PIECE_TYPES`, add a `PIECES` palette entry and icon, add a `'curve'` case in `buildPiece()`, and include it in the challenge decoder’s `VALID` set.
2. Implement a fixed-shape quarter-turn curve in `game.js`: generate a **flat ribbon mesh** following an arc (for example, with a custom `BufferGeometry` or an extruded annular shape), oriented by `p.r`. A flat drivable surface is preferable to a tube-shaped mesh.

Add them through `addColliderBox()` with `kind: 'platform'`; the existing broadphase and sphere-versus-box response can then process them without a new collision branch. This is a practical approximation, not an exact curved-surface collision solution.
4. Give the editor ghost a curve-shaped preview in `applyBuilderCursor()`; otherwise placement will still be represented by the generic box ghost.
5. If the curve has a fixed shape and uses only `r` for rotation, the current challenge serialization already carries the needed fields. If it has configurable radius, angle, or other parameters, those fields must also be explicitly serialized and decoded in `store.js`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarifying questions.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with short overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game, timed courses, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, responsive UI, and map builder.
- Added quarter-turn curve pieces, rendering and colliders, builder palette and preview, and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- Reshaped Sunrise Sprint into a broader route with curves and multiple directions.
- Ran `npm run build` successfully; production bundle still triggers Vite’s >500 kB chunk warning.
- Checked the homepage in portrait (390×844, no document overflow) and landscape (1280×720); no browser exceptions were reported.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/marble-landscape-latest.jpg` (1280×720).

### Active
- Verify curve shape, rotation, collider alignment, and builder placement in gameplay.
- Consider broadening other built-in maps with curves and multidirectional routes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test curve orientation, collision, builder preview, and placement in the browser.
2. Review the final source and generated `dist/` diff.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve rendering, collision, and builder preview/placement.
- `src/maps.js`: Curve piece type and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve icon/hint.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `/tmp/opencode/marble-landscape-latest.jpg`: Latest inspected landscape screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `npm run build` regenerated `dist/`; the current JavaScript bundle is `dist/assets/index-MyU3ADQB.js`, with the large-chunk warning noted above.
- Curve body and surface use `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2`; curve surface material is double-sided.

## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarifying questions.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with short overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game, timed courses, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, responsive UI, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- Broadened Sunrise Sprint with curves and multiple directions; added two curves to Neon Current.
- Adjusted curve collider placement and width to better follow the curved surface.
- Added a curve-shaped builder preview outline that follows rotation.
- Earlier checks confirmed `npm run build` succeeds and portrait (390×844) and landscape (1280×720) layouts have no overflow or reported browser exceptions.

### Active
- Verify curve orientation, collision, builder preview, and placement in gameplay.
- Review built-in map layouts and final source/`dist/` changes.
- Rebuild after the latest curve and map edits; the previous successful build predates those edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test curve orientation, collision, builder preview, and placement in the browser; capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.
2. Run `npm run build` after the latest edits and review the source and generated `dist/` diff.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve rendering, collision, and builder preview/placement.
- `src/maps.js`: Curve piece type and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve hint/icon.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `/tmp/opencode/marble-landscape-latest.jpg`: Previously inspected landscape screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Latest edits are not yet included in a production build; Vite previously warned that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- A map uniqueness check found Sunrise Sprint already has overlapping pieces at `0,-1,1`; account for intentional route overlaps when validating layouts.
- A Chromium screenshot was captured at `/tmp/opencode/marble-curves-check.png`; it is PNG, not the requested JPEG.

## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarification.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with short overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game features, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, responsive UI, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps.
- Increased grid bounds and reworked Sunrise Sprint into a multi-direction course.
- `npm run build` succeeded; output warns that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.

- Review generated `dist/` and source changes.

- `src/maps.js`: Grid bounds, curve type, and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve hint/icon.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `dist/`: Generated production build output.

## Important Context

- Latest curve adjustments: collider arc uses `localZ = CELL / 2 - trackRadius * Math.sin(angle)` and tangent yaw `Math.PI / 2 + angle + baseYaw`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarification.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game features, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, responsive UI, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps.
- Expanded grid bounds and reworked Sunrise Sprint into a multi-direction course.
- `npm run build` succeeds; built-in map bounds/overlap validation and `git diff --check` pass.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG screenshot at 1280×577 while testing the builder’s curve tool and rotation.

### Active
- Verify curve orientation and collision behavior, builder preview rotation, and edited Sunrise Sprint gameplay placement.
- Review generated `dist/` output and source changes; changes remain uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test curve orientation/collision, builder preview rotation, and the edited Sunrise Sprint route in gameplay.
2. Review the final `git diff`, including generated `dist/` assets.
3. Address or accept the Vite warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve geometry, colliders, builder preview, and gameplay.
- `src/maps.js`: Grid bounds, curve type, and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve hint/icon.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `dist/`: Generated production build output.

## Important Context
- Latest collider edits use `localZ = CELL / 2 - trackRadius * Math.sin(angle)` and tangent yaw `Math.PI - angle + baseYaw`; gameplay verification is pending.
- Sunrise Sprint’s last curve now leads through `(0,3,1)` to finish at `(0,1,1)`.
- Built-in overlap checks permit checkpoints sharing a cell with platforms; validation passed for all three maps.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarification.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game features, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, responsive UI, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps.
- Expanded grid bounds and reworked Sunrise Sprint into a multi-direction course.
- `npm run build` succeeds; built-in map bounds/overlap validation and `git diff --check` pass.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG screenshot at 1280×577 while testing the builder’s curve tool and rotation.

### Active
- Verify curve orientation and collision behavior, builder preview rotation, and edited Sunrise Sprint gameplay placement.
- Review generated `dist/` output and source changes; changes remain uncommitted.
- Decide whether to address or accept the Vite warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test curve orientation/collision, builder preview rotation, and the edited Sunrise Sprint route in gameplay.
2. Review the final `git diff`, including generated `dist/` assets.
3. Address or accept the Vite chunk-size warning.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve geometry, colliders, builder preview, and gameplay.
- `src/maps.js`: Grid bounds, curve type, and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve hint/icon.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `dist/`: Generated production build output.

## Important Context
- Curve colliders use `localZ = CELL / 2 - trackRadius * Math.sin(angle)` and tangent yaw `Math.PI - angle + baseYaw`; gameplay verification is pending.
- Sunrise Sprint’s last curve routes through `(0,3,1)` to finish at `(0,1,1)`.
- Neon Current also has two curve pieces; overlap and bounds validation passed for all three built-in maps.
- Vite dev server was started with `npm run dev -- --port 4173`; browser verification had not yet been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a landscape-friendly, open 360-degree park with bigger, cleaner blocks and more curved pieces.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project without clarification.
- Check the interface using JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Make maps feel like large parks players can explore in any direction, not just along a straight path.

## Decisions
- Use a static Vite + Three.js game with `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented responsive landscape layouts, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code support.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps; expanded grid bounds and reworked Sunrise Sprint into a multi-direction course.
- `npm run build` succeeds; built-in map bounds/overlap validation and `git diff --check` pass.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG screenshot at 1280×720.
- Exercised the browser flow from home to official maps and into Sunrise Sprint gameplay using headless Chrome.

### Active
- Verify curve orientation and collision behavior, builder preview rotation, and edited Sunrise Sprint route placement in gameplay.
- Review final changes, including generated `dist/` output; changes remain uncommitted.
- Decide whether to address or accept Vite’s JavaScript chunk-size warning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test curve orientation/collision, builder preview rotation, and Sunrise Sprint gameplay placement.
2. Review the final `git diff`, including generated `dist/` assets.
3. Address or accept the Vite chunk-size warning.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve geometry, colliders, builder preview, and gameplay.
- `src/maps.js`: Grid bounds, curve type, and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Builder palette and curve hint/icon.
- `src/store.js`: `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive and landscape layouts.
- `dist/`: Generated production build output.

## Important Context
- Curve colliders use `localZ = CELL / 2 - trackRadius * Math.sin(angle)` and tangent yaw `Math.PI - angle + baseYaw`; gameplay verification remains pending.
- Sunrise Sprint’s last curve routes through `(0,3,1)` to finish at `(0,1,1)`; Neon Current also contains curves.
- `npm run build` reports a 689.77 kB minified JavaScript chunk, above Vite’s 500 kB warning threshold.
- `dist/` has regenerated hashed assets; tracked old assets are deleted and new ones are untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a spacious, landscape-friendly playground with larger adjustable controls, larger tiles, curved pieces, and multiple routes to the finish.

## Requirements
- Make controls such as the joystick and jump button bigger.
- Make courses and tiles larger and less cramped, with paths players can explore in any direction.
- Provide multiple pathways to reach the finish.
- Add blocks with curves.
- Keep competition local: built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Check interface changes with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the existing static Vite + Three.js game and `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive landscape layouts, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code support.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps; expanded grid bounds and reworked Sunrise Sprint into a multi-direction course.
- Adjusted curve connectors and Neon Current route placements; verified built-in curve connections and collider tangents.
- Previously ran `git diff --check` and `npm run build` successfully; started a race in Chromium with no runtime errors and inspected `/tmp/opencode/latest-marble.jpg` (1280px wide).

### Active
- Increase joystick and jump-button sizes and add a user-facing control-size setting.
- Expand courses into spacious playgrounds with genuine route choices and multiple ways to reach the finish; ensure larger tiles/areas feel less cramped.
- Test curve driving/collisions, builder preview rotation, and both adjusted built-in routes in gameplay.
- Review the production build and Vite chunk-size warning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add adjustable touch-control sizing and enlarge the controls; verify the landscape interface and capture/inspect only the latest JPEG screenshot (≤1280px).
2. Add spacious, branching routes with multiple finish approaches; test curve driving, preview rotation, and both built-in courses.
3. Run `git status --short`, `git diff --check`, and `npm run build`; review the build output.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Curve geometry/colliders, builder preview, and gameplay.
- `src/maps.js`: Grid bounds, piece types, and built-in course layouts.
- `src/main.js`: Settings behavior, builder palette, and touch controls.
- `src/store.js`: Settings persistence and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive layouts and touch-control sizing.
- `index.html`: Settings modal and in-game touch-control markup.

## Important Context
- Latest `git status --short && git diff --stat` returned no output; no uncommitted changes were reported.
- Previous production build succeeded but warned the main JavaScript chunk is 689.83 kB minified, above Vite’s 500 kB threshold.
- Current touch-control dimensions are defined in `src/style.css`; settings currently have no control-size option.
- Curve collider tangent yaw is `Math.PI - angle + baseYaw`; a prior alternative failed the tangent check.

## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a spacious, landscape-friendly playground with larger controls and tiles, curved pieces, and multiple routes to the finish.

## Requirements
- Make the joystick and jump button bigger, with adjustable sizing.
- Make courses less cramped and provide paths players can explore in different directions.
- Provide multiple pathways to the finish and add curved blocks.
- Keep competition local with built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Check interface changes with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the existing static Vite + Three.js game and `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.
- Touch-control sizing offers Small, Medium, and Large; Large is the default.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive landscape layouts, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code support.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps; expanded grid bounds and adjusted built-in routes.
- Increased tile spacing from `CELL = 2.4` / `STEP = 1.2` to `CELL = 2.8` / `STEP = 1.4`.
- Added touch-control setting persistence, Settings selector, UI synchronization/event handling, and responsive size styles.
- Added a Sunrise bypass and a Neon shortcut; no duplicate piece coordinates in Sunrise.
- `npm run build` succeeds; `git diff --check` passed. A prior gameplay session had no runtime errors and `/tmp/opencode/latest-marble.jpg` was inspected at 1280px wide.

### Active
- Validate that new branches provide usable alternate routes and fix the Neon duplicate piece at `(2, 7, 1)`.
- Test curve driving/collisions, builder preview rotation, and both adjusted built-in routes in gameplay.
- Verify control-size settings and landscape UI in Chromium; capture and inspect only the latest JPEG screenshot (≤1280px).
- Review the production build output and Vite chunk-size warning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and correct Neon’s overlapping branch piece(s), then validate branch connectivity and finish approaches.
2. Run the game in Chromium; test routes, curves, builder preview rotation, and touch-size selector; capture and inspect the latest ≤1280px JPEG.
3. Run `git status --short`, `git diff --check`, and `npm run build`; review generated `dist/` changes and the bundle warning.

## Relevant Files
- `src/maps.js`: Tile spacing, curve pieces, built-in routes, and new branches.
- `src/main.js`: Settings synchronization, touch-size handler, and game UI wiring.
- `src/style.css`: Touch-control sizing and responsive landscape rules.
- `src/game.js`: Curve geometry/colliders, builder preview, and gameplay.
- `src/store.js`: Settings persistence and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `index.html`: Settings modal and touch-control markup.

## Important Context
- Latest build reports `dist/assets/index-C4Wf7h-d.js` at 690.48 kB minified, above Vite’s 500 kB threshold; build succeeds.
- `dist/` contains generated uncommitted changes, including removed old hashed assets and newly generated assets.
- Neon currently has a duplicate piece coordinate `(2, 7, 1)` after adding its alternate route.

## Objective
- Expand the existing 3D marble parkour game into a spacious, landscape-friendly playground with larger adjustable controls, curved pieces, and multiple routes to the finish.

## Requirements
- Make the joystick and jump button bigger, with adjustable sizing.
- Make courses less cramped, with paths players can explore in different directions and multiple ways to finish.
- Add curved blocks.
- Keep competition local with built-in rival times, personal-best ghosts, and shareable custom-map codes.
- Check interface changes with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use the existing static Vite + Three.js game and `localStorage` persistence.
- Keep leaderboards and ghosts local; share custom maps through copy/paste codes.
- Implement curves as flat drivable quarter-turn tracks with overlapping oriented-box colliders.
- Touch-control sizing offers Small, Normal, and Large; Large is the default.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive landscape layouts, local persistence, touch and keyboard controls, map builder, quarter-turn pieces, and `MR1` challenge-code support.
- Added curve rendering, colliders, builder preview, and curves to built-in maps; expanded grid bounds and adjusted routes.
- Added adjustable touch-control settings, persistence, Settings selector, UI synchronization, and responsive sizing styles.
- Expanded tile spacing to `CELL = 2.8` / `STEP = 1.4`; added Sunrise bypass and Neon shortcut pieces; fixed Neon route gaps.
- Grid-neighbor validation found a route in every built-in map and no duplicate piece coordinates.
- Chromium smoke test confirmed landscape UI, touch mode, default Large selection and persistence, and Sunrise Sprint gameplay; joystick measured 144px and jump button 115.188px.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/marble-ui-latest.jpg` (1280×720).
- `npm run build` succeeded and `git diff --check` passed.
- Re-ran `/tmp/opencode/validate-marble.mjs`; smoke test still passes, with two unresolved resource 404 console errors.

### Active
- Validate driving and collisions on curves, builder preview rotation and placement, race completion, and Small/Normal/Large control adjustments; only Large was fully verified.
- Investigate the two browser console resource 404s if relevant.
- Review generated `dist/` assets and bundle-size warning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser validation for curve behavior, builder curve preview/rotation, finishing a race, and all touch-control sizes.
2. Investigate the two console 404s and fix any gameplay issues found.
3. Rerun `npm run build`, `git diff --check`, and `git status --short`; review generated `dist/` assets and bundle-size warning.

## Relevant Files
- `src/maps.js`: Built-in map layouts, tile spacing, curves, branches, and grid bounds.
- `src/game.js`: Gameplay geometry, curve colliders, builder preview, physics, and race lifecycle.
- `src/main.js`: Settings and game UI wiring, map flow, and touch-control sizing.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive layouts and touch-control size styles.
- `src/store.js`: Settings persistence and `MR1` challenge-code validation.
- `index.html`: Settings modal and UI markup.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-marble.mjs`: Chromium UI smoke-test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/marble-ui-latest.jpg`: Latest inspected JPEG screenshot.

## Important Context
- Source and generated `dist/` changes are uncommitted. The latest build generated `dist/assets/index-jtXX3ZGZ.js` and `dist/assets/index-tZaefdvg.css`; rebuilding may change hashes.
- Latest build reports a 690.54 kB minified JS chunk, exceeding Vite’s 500 kB warning threshold.
- Dev server is available at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.
- Built-in map connectivity was checked by grid-neighbor validation; physical traversal and curve collisions remain unverified.
